thread:
marco: Heads-up — we still don't have a single agreed definition for TTFT and TPOT across replay vs synthetic runs. This is causing noise in kernel-selection comparisons.

anish: Agreed. Can we lock a canonical measurement matrix? e.g., what to include in TTFT (scheduling, memcpy, kernel) and what to attribute to runtime vs infra.

devon: +1. Also need to control KV cache state — replay harness default keeps warm cache which biases goodput. We should run both ColdStart and SteadyState.

rachel: For clarity, I'm proposing: TTFT = time from request received by serving runtime to first byte emitted. TPOT = time to produce full token output for the request (end-to-end within runtime). Then separate 'net' and 'kernel' breakdowns. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

marco: That split looks sane. We should require a standardized breakdown like: scheduling wait, batching delay, kernel compute, memcpy in/out, streaming flush. Without those we can't compare kernel choices.

anish: Also add an explicit goodput definition. My suggestion: goodput = number of tokens deemed "useful" / sec, where useful excludes padding/retries/failed requests. QPS is just requests/sec. Goodput lets us compare different batching/quantization setups apples-to-apples.

devon: Quick practical checklist for runs I ran today:
- Seed RNGs for model sessions
- Fix sequence length dist to our sampled production trace or an explicit synthetic "50/150/512" mix
- Run ColdStart (KV empty) for 10k requests, then SteadyState for 50k requests
- Capture per-request breakdown and per-kernel timelines

rachel: Can we capture tail latencies per-phase? p95/p99 currently reported as a single number but that hides batching debounce effects. I'd like p95/p99 for: TTFT, kernel-only, batching-delay.

marco: Yes. For the apples-to-apples comparisons we should publish: median(TTFT), p95(TTFT), p99(TTFT), median(kernel), p95(kernel), mean goodput, and KV hit-rate.

devon: Sharing a profiling snippet from perf tool (pseudo):
```
# per-request csv columns
request_id,seq_len,kv_hit,enqueue_delay_ms,batch_wait_ms,kernel_ms,memcpy_ms,ttft_ms
# example row
req42,150,1,0.5,3.2,12.8,0.7,17.2
```
If batch_wait_ms has a fat tail, p99(TTFT) will balloon even if kernel_ms is stable.

anish: Important: kernel selection bench must fix the same batching heuristic parameters. Otherwise the runtime might pick a different kernel because it expects different input shapes. Kernel-level speedups should be measured with identical scheduling/batching config.

rachel: On synthetic vs replay: replay is closest to production but brittle (needs trace sanitization and privacy). Synthetic lets us sweep params like seq-length skew or arrival bursts. Proposal: publish both for each PR and label which one is authoritative for merge decisions.

marco: We need an automated check in CI: for any perf PR, run a small deterministic synthetic harness that verifies no >5% regression in median(TTFT) and no >10% regression in p99(kernel). If non-determinism spikes, fail and require a larger replay job.

perf-bot: perf-run completed: 1849991248. synth-harness (seed=42): median_ttft=16.9ms (+1.2%), p99_kernel=48.1ms (-0.4%), goodput=12.4k tok/s (-0.8%). KV_hit=0.62.

devon: That bot output is good but please attach the raw CSV and the per-kernel timeline. We need to inspect cases where batch_wait_ms > 20ms.

anish: For kernel selection experiments, keep the following constant across variants: same model weights, same batcher config (max_batch_tokens, max_batch_size, batching_timeout_ms), same baseline quantization profile. Then toggle only kernel impl or small kernel tuning flags.

rachel: Also log the cache policy: whether we evict LRU at token or sequence granularity — that changes steady-state hit-rate. Add KV population script to the harness to reproduce warm cache status.

marco: Action items:
- anish: draft a one-pager with canonical metric definitions + required per-run artifacts (csv, kernel timeline, harness config)
- devon: add ColdStart/SteadyState modes and seq-len distributions to the replay harness
- rachel: update CI perf-check to run synthetic quick-check and link to a replay job if thresholds exceeded

anish: I'll also include an example command for runners: 
```
./run_harness --mode=synthetic --seed=42 --seq-dist="0.6:50,0.3:150,0.1:512" --cold-requests=10000 --steady-requests=50000 --report=csv,timeline
```

devon: Perfect. One more: add a flag to force KV_hit_rate in steady state for controlled experiments (e.g., prepopulate N unique keys to target ~70% hit).

rachel: Sounds like we're converging. Marco — can you post the one-pager draft in #eng-runtime tomorrow? Then we can start converting historical run outputs to the new schema for baseline comparisons. :white_check_mark:

marco: Will do. Thanks everyone.
